newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks fall to close below 2,300.
newsitem.headline: French stocks fall to close below 2,300.

text.p: French stocks closed sharply lower on Thursday after the bourse followed a fall in the bond markets and a wobbly start in trading on Wall Street, brokers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 16.15 points, or 0.7 percent, at 2,292.50, while the CAC-40 December futures contract fell 15.5 points to 2,294.50. Volume was 5.85 billion francs.
Analysts say the market was due for a pause after a sharp recent rise that brought the CAC close to its all-time record of 2,360.98 points, set in February 1994.
Brokers said the market gave back its early gains after the central banks of France and Germany failed to deliver anticipated interest rate cuts on Thursday.
With the dollar also weaker, all the trends that had driven the bourse higher were temporarily stalled.
Brokers said investors, foreigners in particular, were also baffled and discouraged by the suspension announced on Wednesday of the privatisation of electronics group Thomson.

Shares in Alcatel Alsthom, whose bid looked to have been rejected in October but turned out to be the favoured candidate of the privatisation commission, extended the previous day's fall, losing a further three francs to close at 457.
Lagardere shares, which were hammered on Wednesday when the government suspended the plan to sell Thomson to Lagardere, staged a weak rebound, adding one franc to 146.
Oil majors Elf-Aquitaine and Total fell 3.06 percent and 1.86 percent, respectively, after Merrill Lynch downgraded its short-term recommendations on their stocks.

Carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen's shares fell 2.51 percent to close at 622 francs. Michelin sold a block of shares representing 2.6 percent of the PSA group's capital at 614 francs per share, but still retains 3.5 percent.

Peugeot Automobiles said on Thursday that it was having difficulties in China and was considering withdrawing from one of its two production sites. On the plus side, however, British car sales for November showed a big rise in its market share.
